card.title: Work
card.says: only the component of a constant force $F$ along the displacement $\Delta x$ does work, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{F}$ and $\Delta\vec{x}$. A force perpendicular to motion ($\theta = 90^\circ$) does **zero** work.
card.from: the dot product $\vec{F} \cdot \Delta\vec{x}$: work measures how much mechanical energy a force transfers into or out of a body.
card.useWhen: a constant force acts on a moving object and you want the energy transferred (for a varying force, take the area under the $F$–$x$ graph).
card.example: Pulling a box with $F = 20\text{ N}$ at $\theta = 60^\circ$ above the floor for $\Delta x = 5\text{ m}$ → $W = 20 \times 5 \times \cos 60^\circ = 20 \times 5 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ J}$.
card.analogy: Carrying a heavy backpack horizontally across a flat room feels tiring, yet your upward lift is perpendicular to your motion, so in physics it does zero work on the bag.
